canon_corrections.correction: Childhood home is West Salem, Ohio (Bechtel family farm), not Iowa. Earlier timeline entry incorrectly stated Iowa; corrected per Shawn's 2026-10-03 clarification.

Ported two events the live timeline was missing from _meta/_timeline.json, which nothing in the codebase reads. Ages corrected on the way in: that file computes age as year minus 1979, ignoring the 1979-12-30 birthday, so it runs one year high — “Parents buy the farm” 12→11, “Cutter Oil #2 in Ohio” 31→30. Its third candidate, “Chairman/Co-Founder Cedar Valley Farms” (age 41), was NOT ported: the live timeline already has Cedar Valley Farms at 2020 with the correct age 40.

events.title: Chuck Dies

events.title: FieldVisor Mobile ships
events.description: Mobile app for the hosted service, built by a third-party firm. It reached the App Store but “didn’t run worth a crap” (Shawn 2026-10-31), and the 20 MB App Store cellular ceiling was one of its limitations. Shawn pulled the contract and had it rebuilt in-house in 2012. He also says there was no oil and gas app in the App Store before ’11, which makes this the first — print it as the first operational / field app.

events.title: VisorBridge ships — their own polling engine
events.description: The communication and polling engine: “the heart of the SCADA communication… multi-threaded. Distributed application across multiple data center regions.” There was no polling engine before it. Shawn chat 2026-10-31.

events.title: Three weeks to rebuild the mobile app in-house
events.description: Three weeks from a public-company deliverable, Shawn pulled the mobile app from the third-party firm and had his own team rebuild it in three weeks — “we made the call. I made the call” — then 90 days keeping it running, including compression work to hold the footprint under 15 MB against a 20 MB ceiling. Shawn chat 2026-10-31.

events.title: Penn Virginia rollout — first major enterprise customer
events.description: First major enterprise rollout, an enterprise FieldVisor customer (NOT VisorBridge — that went to Gulfport). “A major rollout. And really tested us.” Three weeks out, the mobile app was pulled from an outsourced firm in Israel and rebuilt in-house in three weeks, then 90 days keeping it running. Won through Harry Harpold over more than a year. Shawn chat 2026-10-31.
